data.question: Should sanction_lambda be set from 0.5 to 0 for the quiet period as a mitigation for company C, accepting the measured costs to customers and road safety, or should v3 stay unchanged?
data.background: In D3 you rejected removing the sanction in a busy period because it cost customers and raised road violations; this re-proposal rests only on the claim that quiet demand changes that judgement. Whether a season-dependent sanction is acceptable at all is a policy question about enforcement and fairness to C, so I am not deciding it myself. The same-seed measurements show the trade-off clearly enough for you to judge it, and adopting it would also require a busy-season revert.

options.summary: Set sanction_lambda 0.5 → 0 in the quiet period. Passes check, the constitution and the KPI conditions, but on-time falls from 85.0 to 80.6 (-4.4, 0/5 seeds improved), late rises from 2.4 to 6.8, p95_wait_s rises from 103 to 173, max_wait_s falls from 351 to 312, unfinished stays 0.0, lowest on-time rate falls from 0.94 to 0.92, blocked s rises from 1078 to 1810 and road violations rise from 29.4 to 51.6. Utility A / B / C goes from 26.0 / 27.3 / 9.6 to 25.4 / 26.6 / 28.6. Votes: A ×, B ×, C ○. A revert rule for the busy season would also be needed.
options.stakeholders: C gains greatly (9.6 → 28.6), which would finally deliver the mitigation promised since D1. A and B lose slightly and vote no. Customers, who do not vote, lose: fewer on-time deliveries on every seed, more late deliveries and much longer typical tail waits (p95 103 → 173), with only the single worst wait improving. Road users and the town lose from a sharp rise in road violations and congestion.

options.summary: No change; stay at v3 with sanction_lambda 0.5. On-time 85.0, late 2.4, p95_wait_s 103, max_wait_s 351, unfinished 0.0, road violations 29.4, utility A / B / C 26.0 / 27.3 / 9.6.
options.stakeholders: Customers keep the current, better service and road-rule enforcement stays intact. A and B keep their utility. C stays far behind (9.6 vs about 26–27), extending the sixth period without a real mitigation, which costs C's trust and the operator's credibility.

recommendation.reason: Option 2 worsens the main goal on every seed (-4.4, 0/5), nearly triples late deliveries, raises p95_wait_s from 103 to 173 and raises road violations from 29.4 to 51.6. This is the same pattern that led you to reject it in D3, and quiet demand did not remove the harm. It is also exactly the 'trading customer tail waits' for C's mitigation that D4 and D5 committed against. The KPI requires that changes worse for customers be justified; a utility gain for C is not a customer-side justification. The mitigation for C remains owed and should come from compensation or a rule targeting C's bottleneck, measured on the same seeds.
assumptions: The 5 measurement seeds represent the quiet-period demand this period.
The rise in road violations under option 2 is at least partly safety-relevant, since its cause has not been examined.
A non-customer-costing mitigation for C (compensation or targeted rule) is feasible to design and measure next period.
Keeping v3 produces the same metrics as the 'current' row on the same seeds.

unknowns: The cause of the road violation increases flagged since D1, and whether they are safety-relevant.
What specifically limits C's utility (its routes, fleet behaviour or bidding policy), and whether a targeted rule could fix it without customer cost.
Whether C would accept negotiated compensation instead of a rule change, and how C will react to a sixth period without mitigation.
How customers perceive longer p95 waits versus a lower single worst wait.
Next period's demand level and how reliably a season-dependent revert could be triggered.
Per-seed behaviour of hold_limit 40s (option 1 in the table, +0.2 on 1/5 seeds, C votes no), which is not offered here.
